Jiménez is a small company bringing extra virgin olive oil from Andalusia, straight from the producer.

Why Andalusia

It's where a large share of Spain's olive trees grow. You'll find Arbequina there, mild and fruity, but also Hojiblanca, Arbosana and Picual, each with a character of its own.

What we choose

Just a few oils, every one of them tasted. We favour early-harvest, cold-pressed olives: the oil keeps more freshness, grassy notes and that gentle peppery kick at the finish.

How to use them

Raw, most of the time: on bread, tomatoes, grilled vegetables or fish. If you can't decide, the tasting box lets you compare three varieties side by side.

A question about an oil? Email us at davicojairo09@gmail.com or find us on Instagram, @jimenez_shop_fr.

Delivery

Where are orders shipped from?
All orders are packed and shipped from Paris, in a single parcel.

How much does delivery to France cost?
Chronopost home delivery in mainland France is calculated on the weight of your parcel, from €9.01. It's free on orders of €80 or more.

How long does delivery take in France?
Your parcel is delivered in 3 days.

Do you deliver elsewhere in Europe?
Yes, throughout the European Union and to Switzerland. The rate depends on weight and is shown at checkout:

  • Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands: Chronopost Classic, 2 to 3 working days, from €21.60.
  • Spain, Portugal, Italy, Austria, Denmark, Finland, Greece, Ireland, Sweden: Chronopost Classic, 2 to 3 working days, from €25.20.
  • Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Cyprus: Chronopost Classic, 3 to 5 working days, from €31.20.
  • Switzerland: Chronopost Express, 1 to 3 working days, from €56.40. Customs duties and Swiss VAT are payable by the recipient.

The Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla are not served for the time being.

Which currency will I pay in?
Prices are shown in your country's currency: euro, Swiss franc, Swedish or Danish krone, zloty, Czech koruna, forint or leu.

How are the oils packed?
Our olive oils are shipped in suitable packaging to protect the bottles in transit.

Our olive oils

Where do your oils come from?
Our extra virgin olive oils come from several producers in Andalusia, chosen for their quality, freshness and character.

What's the difference between an Arbequina and a blend?
Arbequina showcases the characteristics of a single olive variety. A blend combines several varieties to create a balanced, distinctive flavour profile.

How should I store olive oil?
Keep it tightly closed, away from light, heat and changes in temperature. Avoid leaving it near a source of heat.

Orders and payment

Which payment methods do you accept?
Payment is made securely online when you place your order.

Can I change or cancel my order?
Get in touch quickly at davicojairo09@gmail.com: we'll do our best if the order hasn't been shipped yet.

Returns

Can I return a food product?
For health and safety reasons, opened food products cannot be taken back. See our returns policy for full details.

What if my parcel arrives damaged?
Contact us within 48 hours with photos so we can look into it and offer you a solution.

Any other questions?

Write to us and we'll get back to you quickly.

Our everyday Arbequina. Fruity and lively, with notes of fresh grass.

The taste

Mild on the palate, fruity, with a grassy finish. It never overpowers a dish.

How to use it

Raw on tomatoes, bread or grilled fish, or for gentle cooking. It's the oil you use generously.

At a glance

  • Variety: Arbequina
  • Origin: Andalusia, Spain
  • Early harvest, cold-pressed
Arbequina extra virgin olive oil, fruity and mild. Harvested early and cold-pressed in Andalusia. Shipped from Paris.

t7.value: Arbequina Extra Virgin Olive Oil, First Harvest

Where does it come from? This Arbequina Extra Virgin olive oil comes from the same Andalusian olive groves, harvested early and cold-pressed to keep all the freshness of the fruit. This is our classic bottle, without specific ecological certification, but made to the same high standards at the press.

The taste: fruity and round, with notes of green apple and almond, a slight bitterness and a subtle peppery finish, the sign of a really fresh oil.

How to enjoy it: preferably raw, as a dressing, to preserve its aromas and nutritional qualities.

What to pair it with: seasonal tomatoes, rustic country bread, grilled vegetables or a fish carpaccio.
Arbequina first harvest: green apple, almond and a gentle peppery kick. Cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil from Andalusia. Shipped from Paris.
